newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian brewer says beer industry faces collapse.
newsitem.headline: Russian brewer says beer industry faces collapse.

text.p: One of Russia's leading brewers said on Tuesday the country's beer industry could collapse if the government did not repeal a law which will put beer in the same category as vodka and other strong drinks.

Vladimir Ulanov, general director of Moscow's Tryokhgorny brewery, said the decision would put more pressure on Russian beer makers at a time when they were confronted with increasing imports and a simultaneous drop in demand.
"On January 1 next year all Russian brewers could simply be forced to stop producing beer," he told a news conference, adding that the country's major brewers would unite to lobby the government.
In a bid to stamp down on the widespread illegal production of alcohol, the government passed legislation in July which put beer, vodka and other strong drinks into the same category.
The law, which comes into effect on January 1, will require producers to apply for a special licence as well as attaching a special seal to every bottle they produce.
"Beer is not vodka -- we make it in great volumes. Our production line works like a machinegun. We can turn out 48,000 bottles an hour," Ulanov said.

"We are not ready for this law and we do not have the machinery to comply with it. We'll have to take on an army of people to add the seals by hand, which will immediately cut production by 75 percent."

Ulanov said the new legislation would add 600 roubles (11 cents) on average to the price of a bottle of Russian beer, making it almost as expensive as the cheaper imported brands which sell for around 4,500 roubles (83 cents).
This could spell doom for Russia's 600 brewers, already under pressure from foreign beers and burdened with high taxes.
"At the moment we are only competing with foreign brands because our beer is cheaper," Ulanov said.

Although alcohol imports are generally falling, beer is the notable exception -- imports were up 31 percent to 133 million litres in the first seven months of this year compared to the same 1995 period.

Russian beer production fell by 104 million litres to 657 million litres in the first half of this year, a drop which agriculture ministry officials blame on a sharp rise in energy prices and outdated equipment.

Beer production in 1990 totalled 3.34 billion litres but by 1995 output had slipped to 1.77 billion litres, thanks partly to a drop in demand. Average consumption is now just 12 litres per person a year, half the 1990 level.
Ulanov said his brewery had attracted a great deal of foreign interest but said the lack of investment guarantees had deterred potential partners.
Overall, Russian officials estimate the brewing industry needs a total of eight trillion roubles ($1.5 billion) to modernise its equipment.
